sentiment.rationale: Guidance was lowered: organic revenue growth guidance was reduced to 'at least 4 percent' from a prior expectation of 'upper end' of the long-term algorithm, and core constant currency EPS growth was set at 'at least 8 percent', which implies 2024 core EPS of at least $8.15, a 7% increase versus 2023 core EPS of $7.62. Management explicitly cited a 'slowdown in the U.S.' and the Quaker recall as ongoing headwinds. The guidance reduction and cautious forward language drive a negative score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2023 net revenue $27,850 million, a decrease of 0.5% reported; full-year 2023 net revenue $91,471 million, an increase of 5.9% reported. Organic revenue growth was 4.5% in Q4 and 9.5% for the full year.
summary.eps: Q4 2023 GAAP EPS $0.94, up 152% (prior year included impairment charges); core EPS $1.78, up 7% year-over-year. Full-year 2023 GAAP EPS $6.56, up 2%; core EPS $7.62, up 12%.
summary.guidance: For 2024, expects at least 4% organic revenue growth, at least 8% core constant currency EPS growth, a core annual effective tax rate of 20%, and total cash returns to shareholders of approximately $8.2 billion. Implies 2024 core EPS of at least $8.15, a 7% increase versus 2023 core EPS of $7.62.
summary.margin: Not disclosed as a standalone metric; core gross margin growth was 30 bps in Q4 and 60 bps for the full year; core operating margin growth was 30 bps in Q4 and 10 bps for the full year.
key_risks: Quaker Foods North America voluntary recall of certain bars and cereals, expected to negatively impact unit volume, net revenue, and operating profit in 2024.
Slowdown in the U.S. food and beverage categories in Q4, partly due to pricing and disposable income pressures, expected to continue in 2024.
Geopolitical events impacting some international markets, potentially continuing in the first half of 2024.
Foreign exchange translation headwind of approximately 1 percentage point on reported net revenue and core EPS growth in 2024.
Higher commodity costs in certain divisions, e.g., cooking oil, seasoning ingredients, potatoes, sweeteners, packaging materials.
key_opportunities: International business (approximately 40% of total revenue) expected to grow faster than the U.S. business in 2024.
Frito-Lay North America expected to return to profitable volume growth in 2024, with strong commercial plans and increased A&M investment.
PepsiCo Beverages North America margin improvement through portfolio optimization, supply chain digitalization, and G&A reduction.
Innovation and brand relaunches (e.g., Pepsi Zero, Mountain Dew Baja Blast, Starry, Gatorade ecosystem) expected to drive top-line growth.
Away-from-home channel growth as consumer mobility normalizes, with PepsiCo investing in distribution and specific solutions.
